items.claim: The 5.4-5.9 span is correctly bounded by the opening first-person formula and the closing neum-YHWH tag, with no tier-1 marker at the 5.6/5.7 shift into divine speech to justify a cut there.
items.evidence: Jer.5.4 opens וַאֲנִ֣י אָמַ֔רְתִּי (byte tier, re-collated); the shift into first-person divine speech at 5.7 carries no koh-amar, imperative, or vocative, and a consonantal sweep of Jer.5-6 locates the chapters only koh-amar onsets at 5.14 and 6.6/6.9/6.16/6.21/6.22, none inside 5.4-5.9, so the refusal to cut at 5.7 is correct. The ketiv/qere notes at both 5.6 and 5.7 are disclosed, and 5.7 is quoted at the qere reading; the neum-YHWH claim and the setumah claimed at 5.9 both check out against the ketiv/qere and petuchah/setumah inventories.
tier_citations: skeleton tier (consonantal sweep, koh-amar object, Jer.5-6)

items.claim: The 5.10-5.13 unit is correctly bounded by a fresh discourse imperative at its head and the explicit koh-amar restart at 5.14 that follows it, with no koh-amar or other tier-1 marker intervening to pull 5.13 into the next oracle.
items.evidence: Jer.5.10 opens עֲל֤וּ בְשָׁרוֹתֶ֨יהָ֙ וְשַׁחֵ֔תוּ (byte tier), a fresh command; a consonantal sweep confirms no koh-amar occurs between 5.10 and 5.13, so 5.13 false-prophet verdict correctly remains outside the 5.14 koh-amar oracle rather than being pulled into it. Both cited setumah marks (5.9 as front seam, 5.13 as the row's own close) check out against the petuchah/setumah inventory, disclosed single-witness and non-driving as required.
tier_citations: skeleton tier (consonantal sweep, koh-amar object, Jer.5.10-5.14)

items.claim: The 5.14-5.19 oracle is correctly bounded at a genuine koh-amar restart naming Yahweh of Armies as the speaker, running through the unmarked foreign-nation description and the not-a-full-end qualifier without an intervening tier-1 seam.
items.evidence: Jer.5.14 opens לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ (byte tier), the chapter's only koh-amar onset by an independent consonantal sweep of Jer.5; no koh-amar, imperative, vocative, or date onset recurs before 5.19, so keeping 5.15-5.19 inside the same oracle is correct, and the setumah cited at the row's own close (5.19) checks out against the petuchah/setumah inventory.
tier_citations: skeleton tier (consonantal sweep, koh-amar object, Jer.5)

items.claim: The 5.20-5.24 boundary and its refusal to cut at WEB's translational quotation-mark close are correctly argued from the bytes, but the row quotes English text out of the ketiv/qere verse 5.24 with no ketiv/qere disclosure anywhere in the row.
items.evidence: Jer.5.20 opens הַגִּ֥ידוּ זֹ֖את (byte tier), genuinely echoing the same declare/publish verb pair opening Jer.4.5 (הַגִּ֣ידוּ ... הַשְׁמִ֔יעוּ, byte-verified) and the same blow-the-trumpet pair recurring at 6.1 (תִּקְע֥וּ שׁוֹפָ֖ר / וּבִתְק֨וֹעַ֙ תִּקְע֣וּ), supporting the claimed cross-seam cohesion; the WEB quotation-mark boundary at 5.22/5.23 is correctly identified as translational apparatus, since no koh-amar, imperative, or vocative occurs there in the Hebrew. However, the ketiv/qere disclosure inventory lists Jer.5.24 as a ketiv/qere verse (וירה ketiv / יוֹרֶ֥ה qere), and the row quotes "in its season" out of that same verse with no ketiv/qere disclosure in any field, even though the ketiv/qere notes at 5.6, 5.7, and 6.7 are each disclosed at their own verses elsewhere in this span, 6.7 named even though not quoted at all. The declared disposition treating this warning as inert is refuted: it is a real, if narrow, disclosure gap under the ketiv/qere symmetry standard, not a heuristic artifact.
tier_citations: tier-4 WEB quotation-mark apparatus (non-evidentiary, cited to rebut)

items.claim: The 5.25-5.31 span is a defensible single unit at an honestly disclosed medium_low confidence, correctly keeping the false-leadership capstone with the iniquity charge for lack of any tier-1 marker at 5.30, and correctly treating the 5.29 neum-YHWH tag as non-driving since no fresh tier-1 onset follows it.
items.evidence: Jer.5.25 opens עֲוֺנוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם הִטּוּ (byte tier) and 5.30 opens שַׁמָּה֙ וְשַׁ֣עֲרוּרָ֔ה (byte tier); a consonantal sweep confirms neither 5.30 nor 5.31 carries koh-amar, an imperative, or a vocative, so the false-leadership material correctly stays inside the same span rather than forming an independent unit. The setumah cited at 5.29 checks out against the petuchah/setumah inventory and is properly used as non-driving corroboration only, consistent with the ruled policy that neum closes a unit only where a fresh tier-1 onset follows, which it does not here.
tier_citations: skeleton tier (consonantal sweep, koh-amar object, Jer.5.25-5.31)

items.claim: The 6.1-6.3 opening is well warranted by a genuine vocative-plus-imperative summons that also carries a verified lexical echo of the 4.5 imperative pairing, correctly run through the unmarked siege description without a further cut.
items.evidence: Jer.6.1 opens הָעִ֣זוּ בְּנֵ֣י בִניָמִ֗ן (byte tier); its וּבִתְק֨וֹעַ֙ תִּקְע֣וּ clause repeats the same verb-noun pair as Jer.4.5's תִּקְע֥וּ שׁוֹפָ֖ר (byte-verified), supporting the claimed cross-seam echo as genuine texture rather than an invented parallel. No koh-amar, imperative, or vocative recurs before 6.4, and the disclosed absence of any parashah mark across 5.31-6.3 checks out against the petuchah/setumah inventory (no entry at 5.31, 6.1, 6.2, or 6.3).

items.claim: The 6.4-6.5 cut is grounded in a genuine change of speaking voice from the summons voice of 6.1-6.3 to the attackers own cohortative-bearing battle-cry, bounded on both sides by real tier-1 markers rather than an arbitrary stanza-slice.
items.evidence: Jer.6.4 opens with a fresh imperative cluster (byte tier); its first-person-plural cohortative וְנַעֲלֶ֣ה (and let us go up) marks a self-addressed attacker voice distinct from the imperative addressed to the Benjamites at 6.1, and the setumah cited at the row's own close (6.5) checks out against the petuchah/setumah inventory.

items.claim: The 6.6-6.8 unit is correctly bounded at the koh-amar restart returning the frame to Yahweh's own voice, and 6.8 is correctly kept inside it since its imperative-vocative appeal is grammatically subordinated to 6.6-6.7 by its own purpose clauses rather than opening an independent unit.
items.evidence: Jer.6.6 opens כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה (byte tier) and is one of two koh-amar onsets across Jer.6.1-6.9 (the other sits at 6.9, itself a fresh restart on a distinct topic). 6.8's imperative-vocative הִוָּסְרִי֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם is grammatically subordinated to 6.6-6.7 by its own lest-clauses and addresses the same city already under address, so the row's rejection of an independent onset there is the strongest real rival and is correctly argued. The 6.5 setumah (front seam) and 6.8 petuchah (row's own close) both check out against the petuchah/setumah inventory, correctly typed PE vs SAMEKH without conflation.
